message.reasoning_content:
Kernel uses stable sigmoid via exp(-|x|) in FP32 and div_rn, then cvt.rn to FP16. Correctly rounded FP16 output requires the FP32 value to be correctly computed close enough that single rounding gives the right FP16 result. Likely mostly correct; need to probe exhaustively over all 65536 finite FP16 values comparing to reference (exact FP64→FP16). Also check subnormal outputs and negative x large (x<0 large → exp(-|x|) tiny → value ≈ exp(-|x|) which is small positive → fine, round to 0.5*... fine).

Edge: x negative large: sigmoid(x)=e^x. Kernel computes exp(x) (since |x|=-x) — underflow to 0 fine. x positive large: numerator=1, denominator=1+exp(-x)≈1, value=1. Fine.

Potential double rounding issue: FP32 intermediate then FP16 rounding — double rounding could deviate from correct single rounding when FP32 value lies on ties. But div_rn is correctly rounded FP32; exp is libdevice exp (not guaranteed correctly rounded). For 16-bit precision, FP32 intermediate (24-bit) double-rounding errors are rare but possible when the true value is within 2^-25 of a tie. Exhaustive test over all 65536 inputs will catch.

Record claim, run exhaustive probe.
